chapter: Early New Orleans drummers and bands
title: Chinee, his inspiration; bass drum size; Happy
summary: Chinee of Celestin's Tuxedo band inspired him; he moved from a 28-inch to a 26-inch bass drum; another drummer, Happy, is named.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: He was the only one I can remember. Can you tell us anything about Chiney?
You say when you used to hear him and you?

Well, Chiney, he was a wonderful drummer. He was one of Celestine's original tuxedo drummers. He was a fine little drummer. He was the one who gave me my inspiration. I used to go watch him. I used to go to a club that used to call the Black Gold in a club that called Chiney Town where he would play on 7 and La Salle at the time. He was my inspiration. I used to watch him. He was a wonderful drummer. He could play. He was little and he sat behind those big drums and having those big 28-inch bass drum. He said you could hardly see him behind the bass drum, but you could hear him. I used to watch him and he was the one who got my inspiration to play. Watching him. I used to love to watch him play.
How big was your bass drum when you started at Ludwig that you got the long drum? That was 28-inch. 28-inch.
26 now. Then another wonderful drummer used to play with Celestine. His name was Happy. I used to enjoy him. He was a good drummer too. Is that Red Happy?

Do you remember which Happy? Or is it Happy Gold? I think it's Happy Gold. The last one I was working on here at Paddock. Oh yeah. That's Happy Gold. He plays in Eureka. That's in Eureka. I played him and Henry Red Island.
